articles.title: Michigan teen volleyball player files lawsuit after she unknowingly shared locker room with trans athlete
articles.summary: Briley Lechner told Fox News Digital she had no idea a transgender athlete allegedly shared the girls' locker room after a Michigan volleyball match.
articles.body: A 16-year-old Michigan volleyball player suing her school district says she was frightened to learn days after a match that a transgender athlete had allegedly shared the girls' locker room, telling Fox News Digital she had no idea at the time and now worries about the privacy of female athletes. Briley Lechner, a varsity volleyball player at Monroe High School in West Monroe, Mich., said she and her teammates routinely changed clothes, took pictures and recorded videos in the locker room without knowing that a transgender athlete from the opposing team was allegedly present. "What's very scary is that the day that this happened, I had no clue that there was a boy on the other team," Lechner told Fox News Digital in an interview Thursday. WOMEN WHO FACED BIOLOGICAL MALES IN GIRLS' SPORTS AND LOCKER ROOMS SPEAK OUT AHEAD OF WASHINGTON STATE VOTE Lechner said the experience left her feeling uncomfortable and disrespected, arguing that female athletes should be able to expect privacy in spaces designated for girls. Lechner and her father, Sean, filed a federal lawsuit on Oct. 9, announced by the Thomas More Law Center, raising Title IX and constitutional claims against Monroe Public Schools, the Michigan High School Athletic Association and school officials over the alleged incident. WASHINGTON FEMALE WRESTLER APPEALS TITLE IX CASE OVER ALLEGED ASSAULT BY TRANS OPPONENT TO NINTH CIRCUIT "I personally think that this is a very point-blank situation," Lechner said. "I think it's very straightforward. There should not be males competing in female sports, and so I realized that if my father and I just said, ‘OK, like whatever, you guys declined it, it is what it is, then nothing's going to change.'" The lawsuit alleges that school officials knowingly concealed from the Monroe High School girls’ volleyball team and their parents that a Sept. 9, 2025, match with Ann Arbor’s Skyline High School included a biological male, according to the Thomas More Law Center. COLORADO SCHOOL PARENTS SOUND ALARM AFTER DAUGHTERS WERE CUT FROM VOLLEYBALL TEAM WHILE TRANS ATHLETE PLAYS The lawsuit also alleges that school officials defended their actions, dismissed the family's formal Title IX discrimination complaint and denied them a meaningful opportunity to appeal the decision. Lechner said the lawsuit is so critical because fairness for women hangs in the balance. "This is so important to me, and I want everyone to know that, because we play the sport, us female athletes play the sport, yes, for the sisterhood, yes, for the love of the game, but also girls take this seriously," Lechner said. "Some girls want to play at a collegiate level, and so this is everyone's, like their life sometimes. They put their tears, their sweat, everything into it. And so this isn't just something so little, like, ‘Oh, it's just a high school sport.’ No, it's not, because it's also happening in college places. It's happening everywhere. It's happening in elementary school, it's all age ranges, and so if we allow it in one age range, it's going to continue." AMERICANS CLASH OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES AS DEBATE HEATS UP: ‘JUST GETTING OUTRAGEOUS' Richard Thompson, president and chief counsel of the Thomas More Law Center, echoed similar sentiments. "This lawsuit is about much more than a single volleyball game," Thompson said in a statement. "It’s about whether public school officials can, with deliberative indifference, knowingly sacrifice the rights of female athletes to accommodate a biological male athlete, conceal that decision from the girls and their parents, and then evade accountability under federal law and the U.S. Constitution." In a statement to Fox News Digital, Andrew Shaw, superintendent of Monroe Public Schools, said, "Monroe Public Schools is aware of recent reports regarding an alleged federal lawsuit, though the district has not been served with any lawsuit. We remain steadfast in our commitment to adhering to all state and federal guidelines and laws while upholding student safety. Should legal proceedings be initiated, the district will address the matter through the appropriate legal channels." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Michigan High School Athletic Association told Fox News Digital in a statement, "For many years, MHSAA policy in this area has been crafted to be fully compliant with federal and state law. We believe the claims made are legally unsound, and we will defend that position through the legal process. Due to the ongoing litigation, we will have no further comment at this time."

articles.title: Israeli settlers attack group of European diplomats in the occupied West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli settlers attacked a group of European diplomats in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, one day after a Washington Post journalist was injured in another assault.
articles.body: Israeli settlers attacked a group of European diplomats in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, one day after a Washington Post journalist was injured in another assault. Settlers attacked the group of European diplomats in the village of Taybeh, a Palestinian Christian village east of Ramallah, according to Israeli media and Wafa, the official Palestinian news agency. The diplomats, local media reported, were from France, Belgium and Poland. Belgium’s Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot slammed the attack and said it was a directly related to Israeli policies in the West Bank. “As the occupying power, Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice,” he said in a statement on X. “Impunity for violent settlers must end.” He said the group also included Catholic representatives. Poland’s Foreign Ministry condemned the attack in a statement on social media, saying that they “expect the Israeli authorities to provide urgent and detailed explanations, identify those responsible and ensure that they are held accountable.” “We are deeply outraged by this incident and condemn it in the strongest possible terms,” the ministry said. “Poland has consistently opposed violence perpetrated by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank. Attacks against members of the diplomatic corps are absolutely unacceptable.” CNN has reached out to the foreign ministries of France and Poland for comment. In one video from the scene, a French official, identified as Aulnoye-Aymeries mayor Bernard Baudoux, is sitting on the ground outside a vehicle with a smashed window. In other videos, masked settlers - some armed with clubs or riding all-terrain vehicles - are blocking the roads ahead of the diplomats and demanding identification. Hussein al-Sheikh, Vice President of the Palestinian Authority, called on the international community to hold Israel responsible for the attack. “This is a miniature model of the scale of the daily terrorism to which our Palestinian people are subjected, and it requires a firm international stance that imposes international protection for the Palestinian people.” Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar said he strongly condemns “the severe acts of violence by Israeli rioters.” He said the foreign ministry was in touch with the ambassadors of the countries involved and was assisting law enforcement. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said there were no soldiers in the area at the time of the attack, and the visit had not been coordinated with the military. “The IDF strongly condemns the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Israeli rioters,” the IDF said. Israeli police are investigating. The settler attack on the diplomats comes one day after a different incident in which settlers attacked veteran Washington Post journalist Heidi Levine as she accompanied a group of Palestinians for the start of the annual olive harvest. Levine was hospitalized and required surgery after the assault, during which she said her camera and passport were stolen. She said the assault lasted about 10 minutes, even though she was clearly wearing a protective vest that identified her as press. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has repeatedly downplayed settler violence, tried to cast doubt on the attack. He said that Israel “unequivocally condemns violence against anyone,” but he issued no condemnation of the masked and armed settlers who were seen on video attacking Levine. Despite clear and unequivocal condemnation from Sa’ar and Israeli President Isaac Herzog, who called the attack on diplomats “outrageous and shocking violence,” Netanyahu once again tried to question the veracity of Saturday’s settler violence, with his office saying in a statement on X that “SERIOUS ACCUSATIONS REQUIRE SERIOUS EVIDENCE.”

articles.title: Kenya confirms four more Ebola cases, bringing total to seven
articles.summary: ⁠Three health workers who ⁠treated the country’s first Ebola patient are among the latest confirmed cases.
articles.body:
The Kenyan government says four new patients have tested positive for the Ebola Bundibugyo virus, bringing the total number of confirmed cases in the East African nation to seven.

Three of the new cases were among health workers who treated the country’s first patient, Kenya’s Ministry of Health said in a statement posted on X on Saturday.

The fourth case is a relative of that same patient, who died from the disease, it added.

The relative had been in quarantine since October 6, the ministry said.

This comes a day after Kenya confirmed three cases in the country. The patient identified on Friday was a “primary contact and a close relative of the first and second cases”, the Health Ministry said.

Kenya’s cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), which has recorded more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,300 deaths since it was officially detected in May.

Kenya’s index patient died on October 5 after being ill in the DRC for a month and then flying to Nairobi on October 3. The cases are the first known infections ⁠passed on inside Kenya.

Of the first patient’s 130 contacts, the Health Ministry said 128, or 98.5 percent, had been quarantined – above the global benchmark of 85 percent to break the chain of transmission.

The ministry says it has traced and quarantined nearly all of the first patient’s contacts and there is no evidence that the virus is spreading in the community.

Kenya has reacted quickly by strengthening screening and establishing a hotline for anyone who suspects they may have been in contact with an Ebola patient, but some observers have questioned how the index patient managed to bypass health screenings upon returning to Kenya and make contact with so many people.

Ebola is highly contagious and spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person, including blood and vomit, or through contact with contaminated materials and surfaces, such as bedding and clothing.

The dominant strain in this outbreak is the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are currently no vaccines or treatments. This has complicated efforts to control the spread of the disease.

Research is under way to develop one or more vaccines that work against the strain, and some of these vaccines are already in the early phases of testing in humans.

articles.title: Alligator kills 71-year-old man fishing in Florida
articles.summary: The 3.7m (12ft) alligator reportedly dragged the man into the water where he was fishing near Orlando.
articles.body:
A 71-year-old man has been killed by an alligator while fishing in a park in central Florida, police have said.

The man was fishing near Lake Apopka in the town of Winter Garden when the 3.7m (12ft) alligator came up to the shoreline and attacked him, police captain Michael Mason said on Friday night.

The attack happened at around 17:00 local time (22:00 BST) on Friday in Dr Bradford Memorial Park, a few miles west of Orlando.

Alligator attacks in Florida are relatively rare, despite a population of about 1.3 million across the state, according to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC).

"Lake Apopka has tonnes of alligators in it, so that's not uncommon to see alligators in this part of town at all," Mason said.

The alligator was "removed as a danger to the public" and "dispatched" by trappers, he said.

"Always be aware of your surroundings, always be safe. Local wildlife - respect it, keep your distance," Mason said. "It looks like it's docile, it looks like your Florida emblem, but it can be dangerous."

After attacking the man on shoreline, the alligator then dragged him into the water, the FWC said, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News.

The attack is the second alligator death in Florida this year, after a 31-year-old woman was killed in June while swimming with her friends near Orlando.

Alligators are a common site in many parts of Florida, particularly in and around lakes, rivers, and grassy areas.

Between 1948 and 2025, there were 32 fatal alligator attacks in the state, out of 500 total incidents, according to the FWC.

The BBC has reached out to the FWC for more information.

articles.title: Kolkata pandal stampede: Heavy rush amid rain led to deadly incident - top developments
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: At least 17 died, and 15 were injured after a stampede-like situation errupted at the Sarada Park (Chor Bagan) Durga Puja pandal in north
articles.body: NEW DELHI: At least 17 died, and 15 were injured after a stampede-like situation errupted at the Sarada Park (Chor Bagan) Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata, officials said on Saturday. The incident occurred around 7.40pm at the exit gate under Girish Park police station as heavy crowds gathered amid rainfall.Earlier, police had said that around 35 people were taken to Calcutta Medical College and Hospital (MCH) for treatment.Following the incident, authorities have issued two helpline numbers through the Lalbazar Control Room for assistance related to the incident: 18003455678 and 03322141310.Prime Minister Narendra Modi's office announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh for the next of kin of the dead, while Rs 50,000 to be given to the injured victims of the pandal stampede."The Prime Minister has announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh from PMNRF would be given to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. The injured would be given Rs 50,000," the statement said.What happened at the pandal?According to police, the crowd surge occurred as rain began to fall on Saturday evening. People waiting outside the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal rushed forward, causing some to fall on the road and triggering a stampede-like situation.West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said that at least 17 people lost their lives and 15 were injured, according to news agency PTI.Earlier, in an official update, police said, "Today at around 7.40 pm, a stampede occurred at the exit gate of Sarada Park (Chor Bagan) Puja Pandal, under Girish Park Police Station, due to heavy crowds of pandal hoppers amid rainfall. The Puja Pandal has now been closed to visitors. All injured persons were rescued and shifted to MCH for treatment. As per the information received so far, approximately 35 persons have been shifted to MCH."Administration responseWest Bengal health minister Sharadwat Mukherjee visited the injured at Calcutta Medical College and Hospital. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari and chief secretary Manoj Agarwal also visited the hospital to meet those receiving treatment.Disaster management personnel were deployed at the site, police said. The pandal was closed to visitors following the incident.Leaders' reactionPrime Minister Narendra Modi expressed his concerns over the distressing situation. He extended his thoughts and prayers to the kins and victims who lost their lives, while wished a speedy recovery to the injured."The stampede in Kolkata is extremely distressing. My thoughts are with those who have lost their loved ones. May the injured recover at the earliest. articles.title: US man accused of drugging college student with fentanyl, raping her before death
articles.summary: A 19-year-old New York man accused of giving fentanyl disguised as cocaine to two women in a college dormitory allegedly waited around 45 minutes before
articles.body: A 19-year-old New York man accused of giving fentanyl disguised as cocaine to two women in a college dormitory allegedly waited around 45 minutes before seeking help, while sending pictures of the unconscious victims to his friends, according to court documents.Moises Freire, who was not a student at the Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT), allegedly gave the drug to student Annabel Richter and her roommate at their dormitory in Manhattan's Chelsea neighbourhood on the night of March 18.Both women lost consciousness and were taken to hospital. Richter never regained consciousness and died on March 21, according to the indictment cited by the Manhattan US Attorney's Office.Prosecutors allege that Freire sexually assaulted Richter while she was unconscious. During the delay before contacting campus security, he allegedly sent photographs of the women to friends. One photograph reportedly showed Richter naked below the waist.Freire allegedly told campus security that the women had passed out because they had consumed too much alcohol. Prosecutors also allege that he claimed he had not realised Richter was unconscious until after he had finished having sex with her.At an April court hearing, prosecutor Ariana Bloom questioned that account.“It is truly hard to believe that the defendant, who seemed entirely coherent and sober at the time, who didn’t have any of the substance, who is captured on the security guard’s body-worn camera seeming coherent and sober, didn’t know what was going on when he was having sex with the victim who was completely unconscious,” Bloom said.Mother remembers Richter as a woman full of lifeRichter's family is mourning the 21-year-old, whom her mother, Flavia Rocha, described as a vibrant young woman with a love of music and art.“Annabel was full of life,” Rocha told The Post. “She knew loads about music and art and had a contagious laughter. Her presence filled the room. For us, her family and her friends, she was and always will be, our beloved Bel.”Rocha said she hoped her daughter's case would draw attention to violence against women and help ensure justice for victims.“I don’t want to think of a world in which crimes against women would be too many to count. Bel and I would often discuss how women who suffered violence would rarely have a voice. I hope that Annabel’s story brings awareness, and meets justice.”According to prosecutors, Freire had told the women he was bringing them cocaine from Mexico. Court papers reportedly say he had tried fentanyl a week earlier and described it as “poison” in a message to a friend.Campus security found both women suffering from acute fentanyl intoxication, prosecutors said. Emergency responders administered Narcan, a medicine used to reverse opioid overdoses, before the women were taken to hospital.Freire faces upgraded chargesFreire is being held without bail while awaiting trial, which is scheduled for March 2027. He is due back in court on October 28 to be arraigned on upgraded charges, including distributing a controlled substance with the intent to commit rape, alongside other narcotics offences.If convicted, he faces a minimum sentence of 20 years in prison and could receive a life sentence.Two other men have also been linked to the case. Brian Peralta Cabrera, 18, of Queens, was separately charged with narcotics conspiracy over allegations that he helped Freire obtain the fentanyl. Harry Rosales Pino has pleaded guilty to distributing narcotics resulting in death.Lawyers representing the three men did not immediately respond to requests for comment, according to the report.Freire's lawyer previously told the court that he had been in a consensual “sexual relationship” with Richter during the year before her death. The allegation of rape and the other charges against Freire remain matters for the courts to determine.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Former US ambassador says South Korea prosecuted him over speech made on American soil
articles.summary: Ambassador Morse Tan faces trial in South Korea over comments he made about crimes allegedly committed by its president, claims Korean authorities have refuted.
articles.body: A former U.S. diplomat appeared in court in South Korea Friday facing charges of defamation against President Lee Jae Myung for comments made on American soil in a case that has left him stranded in the Asian country. Morse Tan's troubles began after he delivered a talk in June 2025 at the National Press Club in Washington, D.C., and responded to a question where he brought up the South Korean leader's alleged involvement in a crime as an adolescent. Since visiting the country in May, Tan has not been allowed to leave due to the case against him, having been charged under the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection, etc., and the Criminal Act. Tan issued his remarks about Lee’s alleged juvenile crimes at a National Press Club event titled: "Report on Election Fraud in the June 3 South Korean Presidential election." In response to a question about President Lee and other issues, Tan responded by citing allegations from a few years back that Lee was involved in a gang rape and murder when he was a teenager. He added that Lee, now 62, was sent to a juvenile detention center and did not complete junior high and high school. SOUTH KOREAN PRESIDENT JUMPS TO INVEST IN MILITARY AFTER TRUMP CUTS JOINT EXERCISES South Korean prosecutors say the criminal allegations against Lee are unsubstantiated, according to the Korea JoongAng Daily. The outlet wrote that they said Lee had not "been prevented from attending middle or high school due to such a criminal record." Another South Korean news outlet, KBS World reported that "the prosecution previously verified that there was no record of Lee’s being incarcerated at a juvenile detention center and concluded that the rumors about his incarceration were false." Asia Business Daily reported that Tan's attorney said that "Even if jurisdiction is recognized, the statements did not present false information, and Tan was not aware that they were false," adding, "He had no intention to defame." Tan told Fox News Digital on Friday that he "pleaded not guilty because I believe that Lee Jae Myung is guilty" during his hearing at the Seoul Central District Court. OVER 50 HOUSE MEMBERS ACCUSE SOUTH KOREA'S NEW LEFT-WING GOVERNMENT OF ATTACKING US COMPANIES, FAVORING CHINA Tan, who has taught constitutional law and served as the dean of Liberty University’s law school, told Fox News Digital his "protected speech is about as protected as it gets." He said South Korea’s prosecutor invoked "criminal defamation, a dubious category which does not exist in the U.S.," to prosecute him. A spokesperson for the South Korean Embassy in Washington, D.C. told Fox News Digital, "This case is being handled in accordance with the relevant laws and regulations, established principles and due process in the Republic of Korea and the restriction on departure is also imposed and reviewed accordingly." Tan says he is disappointed that the U.S. Ambassador to South Korea, Michelle Steel, a former Republican congresswoman from California, has not publicly commented on Tan’s legal case — both Steel and Tan are Korean-Americans. A U.S. State Department spokesperson declined to comment on the specifics of the case. "The Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans," the spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "Due to privacy and other considerations, we have nothing further to share at this time." Tan said the case against him violated his due process rights, and the South Korean judicial system lacks jurisdiction to bring the case. He added that the second charge against him involves his July 2025 talk in South Korea, where he "raised some issues as questions" involving the president. "This is political lawfare. This is a persecution, not a prosecution," he said. TRUMP SHOULD PRESS XI ON CHINA’S PERSECUTION OF BELIEVERS AT HOME AND ABROAD Tan believes the motivation for seeking to criminalize his free speech stems from the South Korean government’s view of him as a "threat" and an outspoken critic of Lee’s alleged appeasement policy toward the North Korean communist regime. "People consider me to be leading a movement against the communizing of South Korea," Tan said. Tan accused the present government of being aligned with North Korean and Chinese communist regimes "against the U.S. and the Korean people." Tan points to bias against him by South Korean authorities, who he says prohibited him from attending the funeral of his grandmother, while it allows South Korean prisoners to attend funerals for family members. KBS World reported that the "Police, who had initially decided not to hand over Tan’s case to the prosecution, launched a reinvestigation at the prosecution’s request." According to South Korean law, Tan could face a prison term if found guilty.

articles.title: Pope Leo returns to Vatican after lung cancer surgery
articles.summary: Doctors say they are seeing ‘continued improvement’ after the US-born pope had a lump removed from his lung on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Pope Leo has returned to the Vatican, four days after receiving surgery for lung cancer in Rome.

The pope said he was feeling “much better” when asked about his health as he was driven away from the Gemelli University Hospital against cries of “holiness” from onlookers on Saturday.

Leo had the lower lobe of his right lung removed on Tuesday. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, which is the most common type of lung cancer.

He is set to resume some duties on Sunday, when he greets the faithful with the Catholic Church’s traditional Angelus blessing.

Doctors have said tests confirmed his “continued improvement”.

Since having surgery, the pope has had a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, held meetings with senior aides and celebrated mass in a makeshift hospital chapel.

Leo thanked staff in the Rome hospital for the work they do every day “taking care of the sick in their fragility”, as well as for “what they had done for him”, a Vatican spokesperson said.

Pope Leo’s next major engagement is a trip to Latin America in mid-November, giving him about three weeks to recover for an ambitious journey that includes a dozen flights and two helicopter trips.

Leo is the first pope from the United States, hailing from Chicago. However, he has spent decades living and working across South America and is a naturalised Peruvian citizen.

articles.title: America's softest generation isn't the kids — it's their parents
articles.summary: Recent incidents of brawls at youth sporting events between coaches and parents raise the real question about who the title of "softest generation" really belongs to.
articles.body: The biggest babies at a girls' flag football tournament in Revere, Massachusetts, weren't the girls. They were the grown men running the game. A coach and referee got into a fight in front of children who had come to play football, not watch two adults lose their tempers. Both men later apologized, but what kind of example were they setting? We hear plenty about how soft kids have become. They can't handle losing, expect trophies for showing up and need constant praise. But as a psychotherapist, I wonder whether we've been blaming the wrong people. Maybe the problem isn't that children can't handle disappointment. Maybe it's that their parents can't stand watching them experience it. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Spend a Saturday at a youth sporting event and you'll see parents screaming at referees and treating a missed call like a personal insult. A father tells his son to stop making excuses after striking out, then berates the umpire. A mother tells her daughter to be a good sport, then complains that the coach didn't give her enough playing time. These are often the same people complaining that America is raising a generation of wimps. Yet the moment a referee makes a call they don't like, they behave like toddlers. A parent who would punish his child for screaming at a teacher may have no problem screaming at a referee. He sees nothing wrong with it because he believes he's standing up for his kid. But defending your child doesn't give you a free pass to behave like a bully. YOUTH FOOTBALL COACHES FIGHTING & ACTING LIKE FOOLS IN PENNSYLVANIA ISN'T THE LEAST BIT SHOCKING For some parents, their child's athletic success has become tied to their own self-esteem. When the child wins, they feel successful. When the child loses, they feel embarrassed. A father who never made varsity may see his son's benching as another personal rejection. The child is playing a game, but the parent is still trying to settle something from 25 years ago. Your child's athletic career isn't a second chance at your own. If you didn't make varsity in high school, screaming at your son's Little League coach isn't going to change that. Youth sports have become an expensive business. Families spend thousands on travel teams, private lessons and tournaments. Some start talking about college scholarships before their children are even teenagers. After all that investment, parents can begin to feel they're owed something. If their child isn't starting, the coach must be playing favorites. If the team loses, someone must be incompetent. Sometimes your kid just isn't that good. Sometimes he has a lousy game. Sometimes the other team is better. That's sports, and arguing with the coach won't change it. We've gotten so used to treating children's disappointment as something that needs fixing that ordinary setbacks have become emergencies. Losing isn't a crisis. Sitting on the bench isn't trauma. A coach telling your kid he needs to improve isn't abuse. Yet some parents respond as though their children have suffered a serious injustice. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! A child who gets benched may be upset for an hour or two. He complains on the ride home, and moves on. His father, meanwhile, is still angry three days later, replaying the coach's decisions. The kid who struck out has forgotten about it. Dad is still furious on Tuesday. These parents are depriving their children of some of the most useful experiences sports can provide. Kids need to learn that trying hard doesn't guarantee winning, that someone else may be better and that unfair things sometimes happen. They need to figure out what to do when they're disappointed rather than expect an adult to intervene. I've seen adults struggle with this same habit. They get passed over for a promotion and assume the boss has something against them. They receive criticism and spend days complaining about how unfairly they've been treated. They devote more energy to proving somebody else was wrong than considering what they might do differently. Of course, parents should intervene when a coach is abusive or a child is genuinely being mistreated. But not making the starting lineup isn't mistreatment. Neither is losing a game or being told to practice more. There's a difference between protecting children from harm and protecting them from disappointment. Which brings us back to Massachusetts. Whatever prompted the disagreement, two adults at a children's football tournament ended up fighting in front of the players. Had one of the girls behaved that way, she probably would have been removed from the game. Instead, the adults were the ones who needed to be separated. Maybe the next time we complain that kids today can't handle disappointment, we should look at the adults standing on the sidelines. If your child's Little League game can ruin your entire weekend, your child isn't the one who needs to grow up.

articles.title: Terror groups are handing Venezuela’s critical minerals over to China
articles.summary: The Trump administration must address the corruption of the Venezuelan government and its role in allowing terrorist organizations and cartels to fund themselves by smuggling critical minerals to Chinese buyers.
articles.body:
The largest armed presence inside Venezuela today isn’t Venezuelan at all — it’s Colombia’s ELN and FARC militia dissidents, who control vast stretches of the border region in a brutal war for territory.

To pay for guns and grenades, these Colombian terrorist organizations are plundering Venezuela’s critical minerals and selling them to Chinese buyers for big profits. More than 56,000 people have been displaced, fleeing the bloodshed.

Speaking from Barranquilla, Colombia last month, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said these “terrorist organizations … operate with impunity” in the border region “entering [Colombia] committing crimes, murders, and attacks, and then returning and hiding in [Venezuela].” To help Colombia’s new government crack down on terrorists, however, the Trump administration must put pressure on the corrupt Venezuelan officials providing them protection .

It is time for America to take decisive action against the corrupt government of interim President Delcy Rodríguez. Rubio’s remarks were a welcome moment of clarity from an administration that too often has treated the Rodríguez government as a security partner rather than as the landlord of the region’s most dangerous terrorist safe haven. Venezuela’s cartels, like Tren de Aragua — which authorized its members to kill U.S. law enforcement officials — are also making big money from gold and critical minerals.

Across southern Venezuela’s Orinoco region, officials and military commanders partner with terrorists, cartels, and “sindicatos” — Venezuela’s mining-territory crime syndicates — providing trading permits, fuel and access to equipment for a bribe. These groups are given free rein to extract mineral resources: tin, rare earths and coltan — essential inputs for jet engines, data centers, nuclear reactors, and military systems.

These minerals aren’t headed for the U.S. defense sector, however. Instead, Chinese intermediaries line up to buy the illicit minerals at high prices. Armed groups smuggle the extracted minerals to ports where they can be shipped to China. Some go through the port of La Guaira, where corrupt officials provide falsified export paperwork. Most of the minerals are sent via the Colombian border, in official vehicles at legal crossings, or in canoes packed with up to 20 tons of raw ore, paying off military officials along the way.

Every shipment of illicit critical minerals that Venezuelan criminal groups sell to Chinese buyers increases Beijing’s mineral processing chokehold and weakens America’s economic security. Venezuela’s abundant minerals and rare earths could help America break China’s monopoly, while driving U.S. investment into Venezuela. Those opportunities are lost if the Trump administration continues to disregard the collaboration of corrupt Venezuela officials and the terrorists.

All of this undermines American interests in the region. U.S. government regulations meant to encourage investment are compounding the problem. Washington has issued sanctions carveouts that allow U.S. companies to buy Venezuelan gold and minerals. But these “licenses” assume that a legitimate mineral market exists. It does not.

Because virtually all Venezuelan minerals are illicitly produced, money under the license is certain to be diverted to criminal groups, giving a veneer of legitimacy to terror financing. The Treasury Department even exempted U.S. banks from complying with the Bank Secrecy Act in Venezuela — a clear admission that the economy is too opaque to police.

Still, American businesses are sitting on the sidelines. To push things forward, the Trump administration mediated a deal to bring hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Venezuelan gold to the U.S. But given the likely linkages to criminal gangs and corrupt officials, no refiners are willing to purchase the gold. Instead, criminal groups are getting paid while American taxpayers are left holding the bag.

Under these circumstances, meaningful U.S. private sector investment is unlikely. Instead of creating the conditions for high-integrity American firms to operate, the Trump administration’s policy of protecting Delcy Rodriguez is boosting “ask-no-questions” Chinese buyers, while shielding criminal groups, encouraging rampant bribery, and watching passively as a flood of illicit mining cash funds the region’s terrorism and violence.

The choice is in Washington’s hands: keep backing the Rodriguez regime while it shelters terrorists and turns a blind eye to Beijing-bound critical minerals or start treating Venezuela’s corrupt and criminal ecosystem itself as the target. As Rubio said, the current situation is “not sustainable. We have to confront it.”

Josh Birenbaum is deputy director of the Center on Economic and Financial Power at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies. Cristina Vollmer Burelli is founder of the advocacy group SOSOrinoco , which documents and denounces illegal mining in Venezuela.

articles.title: Former California mayor pushes guaranteed income as fix for affordability crisis
articles.summary: Michael Tubbs and Mayors for Guaranteed Income push direct cash payments as the fastest fix for the U.S. affordability crisis amid growing state bans.
articles.body: The architect behind the nation's growing movement for no-strings-attached cash pilot programs is doubling down on direct payments, arguing that unconditional cash transfers are the fastest route to easing the burden of high living costs. "Giving families direct, unrestricted cash is the fastest way to address the affordability crisis," the advocacy group Mayors for a Guaranteed Income declared in a recent video on X. "Data from pilots across the country show that guaranteed income works. It's time for us to get to work and make it a reality." Former Stockton, California, Mayor Michael Tubbs — founder of Mayors for a Guaranteed Income — argued in an accompanying video that traditional economic solutions fail to provide immediate relief to struggling families. According to Tubbs, "half of U.S. states saw some kind of guaranteed income legislation introduced" this year. "At a time when key federal aid programs are being dismantled, state leaders are picking up the slack and looking for ways to bolster economic stability for residents. Ultimately, I believe this needs to become a federal intervention, and we are building the momentum needed to earn that kind of national support," he told Fox News Digital. AS AMERICANS ARE CRUSHED BY AFFORDABILITY, GROWING TREND OF MAYORS PUSHING CASH HANDOUTS AS THE ANSWER Americans nationwide have struggled to grapple with rising costs of living, healthcare, and gas prices. "The U.S. is unaffordable for almost all of us," Tubbs said. "Yet, so many solutions about affordability focus on the importance of long-term solutions, like building more affordable housing or breaking up monopolies. But people also need relief now." Tubbs' comments coincided with an Oct. 13 celebration hosted by the group and Alameda, California, city leaders marking the completion of "Rise Up Alameda," the city's first guaranteed income pilot project. City staff presented the program's final 24-month evaluation report to the Alameda City Council on Oct. 6. The Alameda City Council previously allocated $4.6 million in federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds to finance the program, which provided 150 low-income households with $1,000 per month over two years. "Guaranteed income is a proven tool to help our most vulnerable residents achieve financial stability," Alameda Mayor Marilyn Ezzy Ashcraft said. "I am proud that Alameda launched this critical program when families need it most." Ashcraft also provided a statement to Fox News Digital on Friday. "As Mayor of the City of Alameda, one of 14 cities in Alameda County, I am focused on the health and wellbeing of residents of the City of Alameda," she said. ALBUQUERQUE USES WEED TAX TO FUND 'NO-STRINGS-ATTACHED' GUARANTEED INCOME, SPARKING POLICY DEBATE According to the city’s official site, the pilot aimed to "reduce economic instability for program participants, help to change local narratives and perceptions surrounding poverty and the provision of public benefits, and help to support and inform the national discussion regarding public benefits and anti-poverty policies." "There are now more than 30 independent, scientifically-rigorous studies, including around 10,000 recipients of guaranteed income; this is the largest body of research ever amassed on guaranteed income. Very few policies have been this studied this thoroughly before being implemented at scale," Tubbs told Fox News Digital on Friday. He added, "Data is important, but it's only part of our strategy. It's also crucial that people hear from the recipients of guaranteed income, and understand the real life impacts of this kind of unconditional support. As the affordability crisis squeezes working families and an increasingly large majority of Americans struggle to make ends meet, polling shows a bipartisan majority support guaranteed income as an intervention." Mayors for a Guaranteed Income, a coalition of more than 150 mayors, advocates for direct taxpayer-funded stipends as a tool to tackle poverty and economic insecurity. The network has supported dozens of local pilots nationwide since launching in 2020. Cook County, Illinois, recently became the first county government in the nation to make guaranteed cash payments a permanent line item in its budget following an initial ARPA-funded trial. BALTIMORE MAYOR BACKS BALLOT MEASURE CREATING TAXPAYER-FUNDED 'BABY FUND' FOR NEWBORN FAMILIES Tubbs launched one of the nation's earliest municipal cash experiments in Stockton in 2019 and has long maintained that federal tax dollars should supplement income for lower-income households. However, local leaders face funding challenges as the Dec. 31, 2026, deadline to spend most obligated federal pandemic relief funds approaches, potentially leaving cities with budget shortfalls if other funding sources do not replace the expiring aid. At the same time, Republican state officials and conservative policy groups have sought to block guaranteed income programs. Critics argue unconditional handouts discourage work, increase dependence on government assistance and misuse taxpayer funds. TRUMP-BACKED FIREBRAND WINS ARIZONA GOP GOVERNOR PRIMARY, SETTING UP HIGH-STAKES SHOWDOWN Four states — Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, and South Dakota — have passed state laws banning local governments from administering unconditional cash transfers. A similar ban took effect in Kansas after passing without the governor's signature. In Texas, Attorney General Ken Paxton successfully challenged Harris County's "Uplift Harris" cash program in court, resulting in the Texas Supreme Court blocking the direct payments. Conversely, Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs vetoed GOP-led legislation in her state that would have barred municipal guaranteed income initiatives. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Appropriate measures must be taken by both the Union and the state governments irrespective of factors behind it,” Thirumavalavan said.On reports that the BJP-led Union govt was planning for a special Parliament session to pass the controversial delimitation bill, the VCK leader insisted the existing number of MPs be retained, and there is no need to increase the number. articles.title: Rs 100 per km, yet no guarantee of a ride in rain & traffic in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru cabs hit Rs 100/km as rain, traffic and surge pricing push up long weekend fares; cancellations, long waits and no ride guarantee persist.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Rs 100 per kilometre or more was the price commuters were effectively paying for an AC cab in Bengaluru as rain, traffic congestion and surge pricing drove up fares during the ongoing long weekend. With cabs hard to find, many commuters were left waiting for rides, dealing with frequent cancellations or opting for more expensive alternatives.A reality check by TOI on major cab aggregator apps Saturday evening showed that a short, roughly 2-km ride from Residency Road to Church Street cost Rs 221 for an AC cab and Rs 202 for a non-AC cab on Uber. An autorickshaw ride was priced at Rs 105.Rapido quoted Rs 272 for an AC cab, Rs 255 for a non-AC cab and Rs 96 for an autorickshaw. Namma Yatri was relatively cheaper, with an AC cab costing Rs 200, a non-AC cab Rs 196 and an autorickshaw Rs 66 for the same journey.On both Friday and Saturday, premium or priority options for AC cabs and autorickshaws cost at least Rs 30-40 more than the fares quoted for regular options. The higher fares did not necessarily guarantee a quicker ride. Waiting times were at least six to 10 minutes in most cases. Frequent cancellations added to the commuters’ woes.Two major sporting events in the Central Business District (CBD) Saturday — the India-West Indies cricket match and the Bengaluru FC-Chennaiyin FC football match — added to the demand for cabs and to waiting times. Rain that began in the evening also affected cab availability in other parts of the city.“I had to travel from Tumakuru Road to Seshadripuram when it started raining. I checked two apps, and Uber’s AC cab fare was almost Rs 100 more than Rapido’s. However, I couldn’t get a ride on either app even after adding boosters. A trip that would normally cost around Rs 250 was priced at Rs 377 on Uber and Rs 288 on Rapido,” said a commuter, Sparsha NM.The surge in fares was evident Friday evening as well, when many residents were preparing to leave the city for the long weekend. The steep fares were not limited to the CBD. Commuters in other neighbourhoods also reported paying nearly twice their usual fares.“I took a cab from Jayanagar Friday evening for a trip that would normally cost me Rs 150-160. This time, I paid almost Rs 300 — double my usual fare. With cab prices so high, I was forced to take an autorickshaw in the rain,” said commuter Sriharsha M.Rides longer than 15km were costing at least Rs 750 – Rs 1,000, depending on the vehicle being booked on both days.TOI reached out to Uber, Rapido and Namma Yatri, but they were unavailable for comment.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: CJP volunteers stopped during Tiranga campaign near Charminar
articles.summary: CJP volunteers were briefly stopped by Hyderabad police near Charminar during a Tiranga campaign; police cited lack of permission, no case filed.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Volunteers of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were briefly detained by police near Charminar on Friday night while participating in the party’s nationwide ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ campaign, organised in solidarity with two party members arrested in Delhi earlier this week.Around 15 volunteers gathered near Charminar and unfurled the national flag as part of the campaign. Similar programmes were reportedly held in Warangal and Armoor. The event was also intended to protest the preventive detention of CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke in Delhi on Friday.According to party members, police questioned the volunteers about permissions for the gathering before detaining them. The CJP maintained that the programme was a peaceful demonstration aimed at expressing solidarity with its members and allowing volunteers to pose with the national flag.“The objective was simple, which is to hold the Indian flag, take a photograph, and express our solidarity peacefully. Why can’t we proudly display our own National Flag in our own country?” a CJP Telangana member said.Charminar inspector T Rambabu said a group of six persons arrived near Charminar around 7.30 pm and sought to unfurl the national flag. “They claimed to be from CJP and wanted to unfurl the national flag. We told there is a procedure and police have to be informed in advance to get permission for any such activity in a crowded public place. Subsequently, they left the place. articles.title: 2 Polavaram supervisors killed in highway crash near Khammam
articles.summary: Two Polavaram project supervisors died and five were injured after a truck hit their Bolero from behind near Khammam’s Wyra mandal; driver detained.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Two supervisors working on the Polavaram project were killed and five others injured when a truck rammed into their Bolero from behind on the greenfield highway exit at Somavaram village in Wyra mandal of Khammam district in the early hours of Saturday.The accident occurred around 2 am when seven employees of a private firm providing outsourced manpower to the Polavaram project were travelling to Hyderabad from Rajahmundry.According to Wyra inspector P Rama Rao, both the Bolero and the truck were heading towards Hyderabad when the truck carrying paper bundles crashed into the SUV from behind.The impact of the collision killed Varikuppala Mallesh (32) and L Upender (40) on the spot. The remaining five occupants of the vehicle sustained injuries and were rushed to a hospital.Police said all seven occupants of the Bolero were working as supervisors on project-related works at Polavaram and were travelling together when the accident occurred.Following information about the crash, police reached the spot, shifted the injured to hospital and initiated rescue and traffic-clearance operations.The truck driver, P Naresh (28), was taken into custody in connection with the accident.
